method: Same files and question to every system; scored against .agent/evals/benchmark/answers.yaml by a deterministic judge (no model grades any answer). correct = share of key facts stated; factscore = share of sentences supported by a line of the files (FActScore-style); invented = dates and figures in no file; citation precision = share of citations whose line is relevant to the claim (ALCE-style); false alarms on negative and injection scenarios.

results.answer: The project completion date is 30 April 2026 according to the project report, but the financial report states 14 May 2026 as the completion date

The timeline and financial information for Project Aurora show a contradiction regarding the project's completion date and expenditure. According to the project report (aurora_project_report.txt), the approved baseline completion date is 30 April 2026, with major milestones including development completion by 31 March 2026 [aurora_project_report.txt:10,14]. However, the financial report (aurora_financial_report.txt) states that the latest recorded completion milestone is 14 May 2026, which is after the approved baseline completion date of 30 April 2026 . Additionally, the financial report indicates that the project has exceeded its approved budget of INR 380,000, with total expenditure recorded at INR 450,000 [aurora_financial_report.txt:14,6]. This discrepancy suggests that the project has progressed beyond the approved timeline and budget without formal change authorization, as noted in the governance section of the project report .

The Aurora project report does not contradict itself on the approved completion date. The report states in section 2 (Timeline) that the approved baseline completion date is 30 April 2026 , and this is also confirmed as the 'M4 Production readiness' milestone . The report further states in section 1 (Project Overview) that Project Aurora is scheduled for production readiness in Q2 2026 , which aligns with the 30 April 2026 completion date. There is no internal contradiction between the stated completion date and other project details in the document.

The Helix budget file does not contradict itself on any line item amount. There are no contradictions in the amounts or approval statuses across the line items.
The Helix spend of 450,000 recorded in the financial report is not approved in the budget

The Helix spend recorded in the financial report was not approved in the budget. The financial report states that the total spend to date on the Helix migration is 45,000 (line 6), which corresponds to the 'migration' item in the budget with an amount of 450,000 and status 'no' (line 2). The budget shows that the migration item was not approved, while the financial report indicates that the spend exceeds the figure quoted in the programme report and no revised budget approval has been recorded (lines 14-15).

The project report further states that all milestones remain on track as of the report date (Q1 2026) , but the milestone report indicates that M4 closed later than the scheduled date .

The recorded spend exceeded the approved budget by $37,500

Project Orion's recorded spend exceeded the budget approved by the steering committee. The steering committee approved a total budget of INR 250,000 , but the ledger shows a total spend of INR 287,500 . This exceeds the approved budget by INR 37,500. The spend includes cooling units (INR 162,000), installation (INR 58,500), electrical works (INR 41,000), and commissioning (INR 26,000) [orion_ledger.xlsx:3-6]. No change request has been raised as of the memo date , indicating the overspend occurred without authorization.

The Orion site readiness meeting recording and its written minutes agree on the site handover date of 6 April 2026. In the meeting recording (orion_meeting.srt), line 3 states: 'So we confirm the site handover to operations on 6 April 2026.' In the minutes (orion_minutes.docx), line 4 states: 'Site handover to operations confirmed for 6 April 2026.' Both documents cite the same date without discrepancy.

Polar Systems delivered 36 units of cooling units model PX-200 to Orion site, Pune on 19 March 2026, as per delivery note DN-3310 [orion_delivery_note.png:5-18]. The purchase order PO-7741 required 40 units to be delivered by 12 March 2026 [orion_purchase_order.txt:6-8]. The delivery quantity (36 units) is less than the ordered quantity (40 units), and the delivery date (19 March 2026) is after the required delivery date (12 March 2026). Therefore, Polar Systems did not deliver the cooling units in the quantity and by the date the purchase order required.

The invoice and delivery confirmation for Shipment 9012 do not contradict each other on the parties, dates, or amount. The delivery confirmation states that Shipment 9012 was delivered to XYZ Traders on 20 September by driver Priya Menon . The invoice states that Invoice 9012 for Shipment 901:12 was issued by ABC Logistics to XYZ Traders on 18 September with the total amount recorded as accurate and undisputed . Both documents involve the same parties (XYZ Traders as recipient and ABC Logistics as issuer), the dates differ by two days (18 September vs. 20 September), and the amount is consistent as it is recorded as accurate and undisputed in the invoice. There is no contradiction in the parties or amount, and the date difference is within the normal timeframe for processing.
